messages:
Alex C: Customer hit a 400 on POST /v1/rerank, says some items completely missing from results and scores look off. Payload they sent below.

Alex C: ```bash
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/rerank \\n  -H \"Authorization: Bearer <key>\" \\n  -H \"Content-Type: application/json\" \\n  -d '{
    \"queries\": [\"How do I reset my password?\"],
    \"documents\": [
      {\"id\":\"doc1\",\"text\":\"Reset flow for account A\",\"passages\": [{\"start\":0,\"text\":\"Go to settings > security\"}]},
      {\"id\":\"doc2\",\"text\":\"Password reset via email\",\"passages\": [{\"start\":0,\"text\":\"Click forgot password\"}]}
    ]
  }'
```

Maria (CS): Do we have the exact error body they got back? 400 messages are usually pretty specific. Also which SDK/version are they using? :thinking:

Alex C: Error body: ```json
{
  \"error\":{
    \"type\":\"invalid_request\",
    \"message\":\"Unrecognized field \"documents\" (at \"input.documents\"). Expected field \"candidates\" or \"items\"\"
  }
}
```

Julian (Eng): This is the crux — the rerank API expects a flat candidates array, not a top-level documents array with nested passages. Also it expects a single `query` (string) for the classic rerank endpoint, not `queries` array. Looks like they're mixing search/document schema with rerank schema. :eyes:

Julian (Eng): Quick checklist: 
- use `query` (string) for the text to score against
- use `candidates` as an array of candidate objects (or plain strings)
- if you have passages, attach them to the candidate objects (not under a `documents` wrapper)
- respect candidate limits (we enforce max 100 candidates per request)

Julian (Eng): Example corrected payload for them to try:```json
{
  \"query\": \"How do I reset my password?\",
  \"candidates\": [
    {\"id\":\"c1\",\"text\":\"Go to settings > security and click Reset\"},
    {\"id\":\"c2\",\"text\":\"Click forgot password on sign-in page\", \"passages\": [{\"cursor\":0,\"text\":\"Click forgot password\"}]}
  ]
}
```

Alex C: Ah — they used `queries` because they tried to reuse search multitask code. I'll ask them to switch. They also had candidates embedded as `documents[*].passages` only, which probably made the server ignore top-level scoring.

Maria (CS): Also flag that if they pass objects in `candidates`, the scorer expects `text` or `content` field on each candidate. If it's missing we default to empty and scores go weird. Can you check sample they gave?

Alex C: Their candidates ended up being `{id, passages}` with no candidate `text` at top-level. That explains missing items in output.

Julian (Eng): Yep — if we can't find top-level text we try to concat passages, but that path is fragile. Best practice: always include a `text` on candidate, and keep passages optional and small. Also watch out for nested arrays: `documents -> passages -> ...` increases tokenization counts and can hit per-request token limit causing partial scoring.

Diane (Support): I'll draft a response with the corrected example and troubleshooting steps: 1) change `queries` to `query`, 2) move to `candidates` top-level, 3) include `text` on each candidate, 4) limit to <=100 candidates, 5) if they need per-passage scoring, flatten passages into candidates with metadata.

Diane (Support): Also asking them to return the full request id header `X-Request-Id` so we can trace logs if they still fail.

Alex C: Customer tried the corrected payload and still sees unexpected score ordering (scores clustered 0.0-0.01). They sent `X-Request-Id: rwd-abc-1234` back.

Julian (Eng): Two follow-ups: 
1) Which model param are they calling? older rerank models had a post-normalization step that could squash scores; use `model: rerank-v2` if available.
2) Can they paste a small reproducible example (3 candidates + query) and the raw response so we can check tokenization and debug scoring?

Alex C: I'll get a mini repro and file it. ticket-bot: create ticket INC-3719 for eng-runtime with the example and request id. :hammer:

ticket-bot: Created ticket INC-3719 assigned to eng-runtime.

Maria (CS): Good. Also adding short docs snippet to the reply: \"Rerank expects `query` + `candidates` (array). Avoid nesting documents -> passages for rerank calls.\" :white_check_mark:

Alex C: Thanks all — sending the repro now and will update the ticket.
